hook: Illia Polosukhin worked as a machine learning engineer at Google, where he contributed to high level APIs for TensorFlow and worked on question answering systems used in Google Search. In 2017 he was one of eight coauthors of the paper Attention Is All You Need, which introduced the Transformer architecture built entirely on attention mechanisms and became the foundation for the large language models that followed. The next year he left Google and, together with Alexander Skidanov and other collaborators, began building a new blockchain protocol out of a small office in San Francisco. That project became NEAR Protocol, a sharded, proof of stake blockchain designed for usability and scalability, which launched its mainnet in 2020. Polosukhin continues to serve as a co-founder of NEAR, and has more recently worked on bringing large language model and AI agent technology into the NEAR ecosystem.
name: Illia Polosukhin

reading.body:
Illia Polosukhin co-authored the 2017 paper introducing the Transformer architecture, which became the foundation for all subsequent large language models, then co-founded NEAR Protocol, a blockchain platform, in 2018.

The Transformer paper represented a decisive shift in machine learning architecture. Before it, sequence models relied on recurrence and convolution. The paper replaced these with attention mechanisms, enabling the scaling properties that made modern large language models possible. Nearly all AI systems trained since have built on this foundation, from GPT to BERT to their successors.

Polosukhin's subsequent work on NEAR Protocol reflects a different set of constraints. A sharded, proof of stake blockchain is designed to solve scalability and coordination problems in distributed systems. This is not about compute for model training. Instead it addresses how compute, resources, and agreements distribute across many machines without central control. NEAR launched its mainnet in 2020, after which Polosukhin has worked on integrating large language models and AI agents into the NEAR ecosystem.

The data does not explain why someone who shaped the architecture underlying modern AI would move into blockchain infrastructure, or whether these interests remain connected.
